Subject: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust / Data handling)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can size the next steps: 

Summary of requirements we heard today:
- Data residency: US-only for customer data (including backups)
- PII classification: certain datasets will be marked as PII and must be redacted/encrypted at rest
- Data retention: FinTrust requires retention of transactional records for up to 7 years for compliance; other data can be shorter
- Logging: access/audit logs must be retained and exportable for at least 12 months
- Support access / break-glass: emergency support access allowed but must be audited with approval workflow and immediate notifications
- Access controls: RBAC with least-privilege roles; ability to create custom roles per-tenant

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether "7 years" applies to all datasets or only a subset (e.g., transaction records)?
2) Please share any standard security contact or email for our SOC team (I have security@fintrust.com listed)
3) I attached a short "Redwood access controls" summary and our SOC2 evidence checklist — Neha will follow up with a technical deep-dive on RBAC and emergency access flows.
4) Would you be open to a technical deep-dive (45–60m) with Neha and Rishi on Wed 4/28 or Thu 4/29?

Attachments: redwood_access_controls_summary.pdf, SOC2_evidence_checklist.xlsx

Thanks — happy to iterate on the summary if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap, looks right to me. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 7-year retention requirement is for transactional and settlement records only. Other user/profile data can be retained per application policy (typically 12–24 months).
- We require US-only residency for production and backups.
- Audit/log retention: 12 months minimum; we prefer they be exportable to our SIEM on demand.
- Support access: we allow break-glass but only with an approval workflow (security approver) and immediate audit trail + notification to our security team.

I've attached our internal security questionnaire (FinTrust_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) separately to the thread for your SOC team.

Weds 4/28 looks good for a technical session; would prefer late morning PT (10am PT) if that works.

Thanks,

Hi Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick responses. A few technical callouts ahead of our deep-dive: 

RBAC / least-privilege
- We support role-based access with tenant-scoped roles (admin, operator, viewer) and custom roles with fine-grained permissions per API/resource.
- Roles are enforced at the API and UI layers; tokens and service principals are scoped to roles.
- Recommended mapping: (Admin = full config, Operator = deploy/run, Viewer = read-only for logs/metrics).

Support access / break-glass
- Break-glass can be enabled per-tenant; activation requires a request in the Console which triggers a security approver flow (configurable approvers).
- When activated, a temporary privileged session is granted with a strict TTL (default 30 mins) and all actions are immutably logged.
- Logs include the approver, requester, justification, session recordings (API call traces), and post-event notifications to configured emails (e.g., security@fintrust.com).
- We also support time-bound encryption key access patterns for emergency support if you use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Data residency & retention
- Hosted US regions: production + backups kept in US-only zones. For additional isolation we offer a Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed networking.
- Retention windows are configurable per-dataset; we can set transactional records to 7 years and other datasets to shorter windows.
- Export: audit logs and raw event data can be streamed to your S3 or SIEM on schedule or on-demand exports.

Logging & evidence
- We can provide sample audit logs and the SOC2 evidence bundles referenced in the checklist (I've attached a sample log snippet to the calendar invite).

Open items for the deep-dive:
- Confirm the exact data classes that require 7-year retention (we need a list to map retention rules).
- Confirm approver email(es) and any internal workflow constraints for break-glass.
\I'll prepare a short RBAC matrix, a sequence diagram for break-glass, and an exportable sample of audit logs. Looking forward to the 4/28 session — Marissa, please send the invite and agenda.
\Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
